examples.label: Query the Winlogon key for stored autologon creds
Values that hold the plaintext password

notes:
=== Windows Autologon and PuTTY Registry Credentials Reference ===
Quick reference for registry-based credential locations accessible to standard users.

=== AUTOLOGON REGISTRY PATH ===
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon

Key values:
  DefaultUserName    → autologon username
  DefaultDomainName  → domain (may be COMPUTER_NAME for local, or DOMAIN for domain accounts)
  DefaultPassword    → plaintext password
  AutoAdminLogon     → 1 = autologon enabled

Query command:
  reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v DefaultPassword
  Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" | Select Default*

Access: BUILTIN\Users has read access — any standard user can read this

Encrypted alternative: Sysinternals Autologon.exe encrypts via LSA secrets (not readable without admin)
Check AutoAdminLogon=1 first to know if plaintext version is in use

=== PUTTY PROXY CREDENTIALS ===
HKCU\SOFTWARE\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions\<session_name>

Key values:
  ProxyUsername    → proxy username
  ProxyPassword    → proxy password (plaintext)
  HostName         → target host
  UserName         → SSH username

Query current user:
  reg query "HKCU\SOFTWARE\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions" /s

Query all users (requires admin or access to HKEY_USERS):
  reg query "HKU\" → list SIDs
  reg query "HKU\<SID>\SOFTWARE\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions" /s

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Autologon credentials on domain-joined machine → domain account → lateral movement
PuTTY proxy credentials → proxy server access → network pivot through corporate proxy
Autologon on kiosk/service machines → often high-privilege accounts for automated tasks
After local admin escalation → sweep all users' HKU hives for PuTTY sessions

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
DefaultPassword value present = immediate credential
AutoAdminLogon=1 with DefaultPassword = definitely in use and readable
PuTTY session proxy credentials = often forgotten and never rotated
Multiple PuTTY sessions per user = each session is a separate credential store to enumerate
